title: Instagram’s Adam Mosseri: If you don’t like AI, ‘then you shouldn’t have it in your feed’
text:
## 事件
- Instagram 负责人 Adam Mosseri 表示不会全面过滤 AI 内容，但用户如果不喜欢 AI 内容，“就不该让它出现在你的信息流里”。
- Mosseri 认为平台应标注 AI 内容而非直接屏蔽，并提议更务实的做法是仅对“相机拍摄的非 AI 内容”做标记。
- 他承认检测 AI 内容越来越困难，随着模型进步，平台可能“失去识别能力”。

## 影响
- Instagram 及 Meta 继续拥抱 AI 生成工具（如 Muse Spark），但未提供用户过滤 AI 内容的选项，可能加剧用户对内容真实性的担忧。
- 标注策略转向“标记非 AI”而非“标记 AI”，可能改变行业对 AI 内容标识的默认逻辑。
- 第三方批评者指出，允许用户将他人数字形象放入 AI 生成内容，可能带来身份造假、骚扰等滥用风险。

## 标的线索
- Meta（META）：旗下 Instagram 和 Facebook 的 AI 内容标注与生成工具策略（待核实）
- 人工智能内容检测/标识技术公司：如 Truepic 等（待核实）
- 社交平台内容治理相关板块：如 TikTok、YouTube 等若跟进类似策略，可能影响内容审核产业链（待核实）

## 待验证
- Mosseri 提到的“为 AI 爱好者提供纯 AI 信息流”是否正在开发或测试中。
- Meta 的 Muse Spark 具体上线时间及实际用户滥用案例数据。
- Instagram 是否会最终改变标注策略，从“标注 AI”转向“标注非 AI”。

Mosseri still doesn’t want to filter out AI posts completely, however. by Emma Roth Close Emma Roth News Writer Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed. Follow Follow See All by Emma Roth Jul 10, 2026, 1:45 PM UTC Link Share Gift Kyle Grillot/Bloomberg via Getty Images Emma Roth Close Emma Roth Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed. Follow Follow See All by Emma Roth is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO. Though Instagram head Adam Mosseri doesn’t want to filter out AI content on the platform, he argues that you “shouldn’t have it in your feed” if you don’t like it. “I don’t think we should filter out AI content,” Mosseri said during an interview on Lenny Rachitsky’s podcast . “I think we should let you know if content is AI content or not.” At the same time, Mosseri seems to be drawing a distinction between content-based sorting and banning AI from the platform entirely. In fact, he believes people who love AI content “should be able to have a feed that’s just AI town.” Instagram, like many other platforms, including TikTok, YouTube, and Facebook, will readily label AI-generated content, but won’t give you an option to filter it out of your feed. Mosseri acknowledged that detecting AI content is “hard,” and that Instagram may “lose the ability” to pick up on AI posts as models improve. “I think you should be able to just ask, ‘Is this AI?,’ and we should be able to tell you we think it probably is, or we’re not sure, or it’s definitely not, or definitely isn’t.” He adds that it might be “more practical” to label non-AI-generated “camera-captured content” instead, echoing what he said about fingerprinting “real media” in December 2025. Related Let us filter AI slop, you cowards Really, you made this without AI? Prove it And while Mosseri notes that Instagram needs to “figure out how to crack down” on spammy AI content, the platform continues to embrace the technology. With the launch of Meta’s AI image generator, Muse Spark, Instagram users can now put other users into their AI creations by just tagging them — a feature that Haley McNamara, the executive director of the National Center on Sexual Exploitation, said “creates obvious and foreseeable opportunities for exploitation, sexual abuse, harassment, and identity fraud.” Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.
